title: Version safety declaration and graceful fallback policy for third-party open models
creator: Aisha Morgan
description: Clarify the required metadata, runtime signals, and rollback/fallback semantics for ingesting unvetted third-party open models into the public catalog. Produce a short, machine-readable 'version safety declaration' schema that callers and runtime can use to determine whether a model can be auto-selected, require soft-pinning, or be routed to a sandboxed pool. Document trade-offs for strict vs permissive acceptance and propose a staged enforcement timeline for new intake policy.
acceptance_criteria: A machine-readable 'version_safety' declaration fields are defined and approved by Applied ML and Runtime teams
Runtime can automatically detect and honor a 'soft_pin' flag; requests routed to pinned variant when soft_pin=true
Fallback chain defined in order: pinned variant -> compatibility-flagged variant -> legacy-safe fallback model, with latency and cost SLOs documented
A minimal intake checklist (behavioral contract, perf smoke tests, KV/seq length compatibility) exists and is referenced from the intake UI and API response metadata
Confluence PRD and the public intake form updated with sample declarations and clear onboarding instructions
notes: 2026-03-01: Kickoff meeting with Applied ML, Runtime, and Security — alignment on goal to reduce silent regressions from unpinned community weights
2026-03-03: Drafted schema proposal for version_safety (fields: checksum, training_provenance_tag, kv_compat_version, soft_pin, expected_max_sequence) — sent to Runtime for review
2026-03-04: Runtime feedback: prefer 'compat_signals' as array of high-level flags (kv_cache_compatible, causal_layer_order_preserved) instead of free text — updated draft
2026-03-05: Trade-off discussion: strict schema reduces incidents but increases onboarding friction. PM proposed staged enforcement: start permissive with telemetry, tighten over 8 weeks
2026-03-07: Security review requested (ticket SEC-3312) for provenance and signature fields — security flagged KMS-backed checksum recommendation
2026-03-09: Design reviewed intake UX mock showing 'safety score' and required fields — design suggested inline help for each signal
2026-03-10: Ready for engineering review. Added acceptance criteria and sample fallback routing config for Runtime team to prototype
follow_up_tasks: ENG: implement runtime honors for 'soft_pin' and compat_signals (ENG-22033)
PM: update public intake form and docs with sample declarations
Design: add inline field help and safety score microcopy for intake UI
Security: finalize checksum/signature guidance and KMS policy (SEC-3312)
QA: create smoke-test harness for new variants and define failure blast-radius experiments
notes_summary: Propose a lightweight machine-readable contract (version_safety) to signal runtime compatibility and enable soft-pinning + deterministic fallback chain. Staged enforcement recommended; security and runtime teams to prototype and iterate.
